title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes and recent hypoglycemia.

HPI
The patient is a long-term patient presenting for a follow-up visit regarding their T2DM. They report that they have been experiencing a hypoglycemic episode on several occasions over the last month. The patient currently manages their condition with both insulin and an oral hypoglycemic medication. They report that symptoms of the hypoglycemic episode include shakiness and sweating. They are seeking guidance on adjusting their regimen to prevent further occurrences.

Medication List
- Insulin (long-term use)
- Metformin (long-term use)

Exam
The patient appears in no acute distress. They are alert and oriented. Skin is intact. Vital signs are stable.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
2. Hypoglycemia.

Plan
1. Continue current insulin and metformin regimen as prescribed.
2. Instructed patient on monitoring blood glucose levels more frequently.
3. Educated the patient on recognizing early signs of a hypoglycemic episode and the importance of immediate carbohydrate intake.
4. Follow up in four weeks to reassess glucose trends.
explanations: Diabetes with hypoglycemia and no coma documented: E11.649.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Hypoglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
